It was also said: (Among them is one who is guided) means among their descendants are those who are guided.

(And many of them are defiant) disbelievers, going out of obedience.

**First issue:** The words of Allah, ﴿Then We sent, following in their footsteps﴾, mean: We followed up on their traces, that is, on the traces of the offspring. It was also said: on the traces of Noah and Abraham, with ﴿Our messengers﴾ being Moses, Elijah, David, Solomon, Jonah and others. ﴿And We sent after them Jesus, son of Mary﴾, and he is of the offspring of Abraham through his mother. ﴿And We gave him the Gospel﴾, which is the Book revealed to him. Its derivation was discussed at the beginning of the Surah of Al ʿImran [see vol. 4, p. 5].

**Second issue:** The words of Allah, ﴿And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him﴾, that is, followed his religion, meaning the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) and their followers, ﴿compassion and mercy﴾, that is, affection. So some of them loved one another. It was also said that this indicates they were commanded in the Gospel to make peace and to refrain from harming people, and Allah softened their hearts for this, unlike the Jews, whose hearts were hardened and who distorted the words from their places. Ra'fa (compassion) is gentleness, and rahma (mercy) is tenderness. It was also said that ra'fa is the lessening of hardship, and rahma is bearing the burden. It was also said that ra'fa is the most intense mercy. The statement is complete here. Then He said: ﴿And monasticism, which they invented﴾, that is, on their own initiative. The best view is that rahbaniyya is in the accusative by an implied verb. Abu ʿAli said: "and they invented it, monasticism, they invented it." Al-Zajjaj said: "that is, they invented it as monasticism, just as you say: I saw Zayd and ʿAmr, I spoke to him." It was also said that it is conjoined to ra'fa and rahma, and the meaning on this view is that Allah gave them these, but they altered and innovated in them. Al-Mawardi said: there are two readings. The first, with a fatha on the ra', is rahba, fear out of dread. The second, with a damma on the ra', is ascribed to the monks (ruhban), like ridwaniyya from ridwan, because they imposed hardships on themselves by abstaining from food, drink and marriage, and by clinging to caves and monasteries. This was because their kings altered and changed (the religion), and a small band remained, who then turned to asceticism and seclusion. Al-Dahhak said: after Jesus, peace be upon him, kings committed the prohibitions for three hundred years, and those who remained on the path of Jesus denounced them for it, and the kings killed them. Some people who remained after them said: "If we forbid them, they will kill us, so we cannot remain among them." So they withdrew from people and took to monasteries. Qatada said: the monasticism they invented was the renunciation of women and the taking of monasteries. And in a raised (marfu') report: "It is their going off to the wilderness and the mountains."

﴿We did not prescribe it for them﴾, that is, We did not impose it on them, nor did We command them to do it. This was said by Ibn Zayd. The words of Allah, ﴿except seeking the good pleasure of Allah﴾, mean: We only commanded them what pleases Allah. This was said by Ibn Muslim. Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿We did not prescribe it for them﴾ means We did not prescribe anything for them at all, and ﴿seeking the good pleasure of Allah﴾ is a substitute for the pronoun in ﴿We prescribed it﴾, and the meaning is: We did not prescribe it for them except seeking the good pleasure of Allah. It was also said that the exception ("except seeking") is disjunctive, and the implied meaning is: We did not prescribe it for them, but they invented it seeking the good pleasure of Allah.

﴿But they did not observe it with its proper observance﴾, that is, they did not maintain it with its due maintenance. This is a particular statement, because those who did not observe it were some of the people. They only used monasticism as a means to seek leadership over people and to consume their wealth, as Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis and monks consume the wealth of people unjustly and avert [them] from the way of Allah﴾ [see vol. 8, p. 122]. This applies to a people whose monasticism led them, in the end, to seek leadership. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the words of Allah, ﴿And monasticism, which they invented﴾, that he said: There were kings after Jesus who altered the Torah and the Gospel, and among them were believers who recited the Torah and the Gospel and called to the religion of Allah. Some people said to their king: "If you killed this group." The believers said: "We will protect you from ourselves." One group said: "Build for us a pillar and lift us up on it, and give us something by which we can raise our food and drink, and we will not return to you." Another group said: "Let us wander the earth and roam, and drink as the wild animals drink in the wilderness; if you overpower us, then kill us." Another group said: "Build for us houses in the desert, and let us dig wells and cultivate herbs, and you will not see us." None of them was without a close relative among them, so they did it. Those (first) people went on the path of Jesus, but after them there remained a people who had altered the Book, and they said: "We will roam and worship as those did," while they were upon their polytheism and had no knowledge of the faith of those who had preceded them whom they imitated. This is the meaning of Allah's words: ﴿And monasticism, which they invented, We did not prescribe it for them, except seeking the good pleasure of Allah﴾, the verse. He says: these righteous people invented it, ﴿but they did not observe it﴾, the later ones, ﴿with its proper observance﴾. ﴿So We gave those who believed among them their reward﴾, meaning those who first invented it and observed it. ﴿And many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning the later ones. When Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ) and few of them remained, they came out of the caves, monasteries and mountain hollows and believed in Muhammad (ﷺ).

**Third issue:** This verse indicates that every newly introduced matter is an innovation (bid'a). Whoever initiates a good practice should persist in it and not turn from it to its opposite, lest he fall within the scope of this verse. On the authority of Abu Umama al-Bahili, whose name was Suday ibn ʿAjlan, who said: You introduced the night prayer of Ramadan, though it was not prescribed for you; only fasting was prescribed for you. So persist in the night prayer since you have done it, and do not abandon it. Some of the Children of Israel introduced innovations which Allah had not prescribed for them, seeking through them the good pleasure of Allah, but they did not observe them with their proper observance. So Allah rebuked them for abandoning them, saying: ﴿And monasticism, which they invented, We did not prescribe it for them, except seeking the good pleasure of Allah, but they did not observe it with its proper observance.﴾

**Fourth issue:** The verse also contains evidence for withdrawal from people into monasteries and houses, and this is recommended when times are corrupt and friends and brothers have changed. The explanation of this was fully given in the Surah of Al-Kahf [see vol. 10, p. 360], and praise be to Allah. In the Musnad of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from the hadith of Abu Umama al-Bahili, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on one of his expeditions, and he said: "A man passed by a cave in which there was some water. He resolved to remain in that cave, where the water in it would sustain him, and he would eat the herbs around it, and withdraw from the world. He said: 'If I went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned this to him, and if he permits me, I will do it; otherwise I will not.' So he came to him and said: 'O Prophet of Allah! I passed by a cave in which there is water and herbs that would sustain me, and my soul urged me to remain in it and withdraw from the world.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'I was not sent with Judaism or Christianity, but I was sent with the upright, tolerant Hanifiyya (the pure monotheistic way). By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, a morning or an evening's going out in the way of Allah is better than the world and whatever is in it, and the standing of one of you in the first row is better than his prayer for sixty years.'" The Kufans narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Do you know which of the people is the most knowledgeable?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "The most knowledgeable of people is the one who is most perceptive of the truth when people differ about it, even if he is deficient in action, and even if he crawls on his backside. Do you know from where the Children of Israel adopted monasticism? The tyrants prevailed over them after Jesus, committing the disobedience of Allah. The people of faith became angry and fought them, but the people of faith were defeated three times, and only a few of them remained. They said: 'If we are destroyed, no one will remain to call to the religion. Come, let us scatter across the earth until Allah sends the unlettered Prophet whom Jesus promised us,' meaning Muhammad (ﷺ). So they dispersed into the mountain caves and invented monasticism. Some of them held fast to their religion, and some of them disbelieved." And he recited: ﴿And monasticism﴾, the verse. "Do you know what the monasticism of my community is? Emigration, jihad, fasting, prayer, pilgrimage, the minor pilgrimage, and glorifying Allah on the hills. O Ibn Mas'ud! The Jews who came before you split into seventy-one sects, of which one sect was saved and the rest perished. The Christians who came before you split into seventy-two sects, of which three were saved and the rest perished: one sect contended with the kings and fought them for the religion of Allah and the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him, until they were killed; and one sect had no power to contend with the kings, but remained among their people and called them to the religion of Allah and the religion of Jesus, son of Mary, so the kings seized them, killed them and cut them apart with saws; and one sect had no power to contend with the kings, nor to remain among their people to call them to the religion of Allah and the religion of Jesus, son of Mary, so they wandered in the mountains and became monks there. These are the ones Allah referred to: ﴿And monasticism, which they invented﴾, the verse. Whoever believes in me, follows me and confirms me has truly observed it with its proper observance, and whoever does not believe in me, those are the defiantly disobedient," meaning those who Judaized and Christianized. It was also said: these are the ones who met Muhammad (ﷺ) but did not believe in him; those are the defiantly disobedient. The verse also contains consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning that the earlier ones also persisted in disbelief, so do not be astonished at the people of your age if they persist in disbelief. And Allah knows best.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 57, verses 28–29:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who believe﴾, meaning: believe in Musa and Isa. (Fear Allah and believe in His Messenger), meaning Muhammad ﷺ. (He will give you a double portion of His mercy), meaning two shares of reward for your faith in Isa and Muhammad, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon them both. This is like His saying: ﴿Those will be given their reward twice, because they were patient﴾. The discussion of this has already been covered [[See vol. 13, p. 297]]. Al-kifl (the double portion) means share and portion. It was discussed in (al-Nisa') [[See vol. 4, p. 295]]. Originally it is a cloth that the rider wraps around himself so that he is not thrown off. This was said by Ibn Juraij. Al-Azhari said something similar, saying: its derivation is from the cloth that a camel rider wraps around its hump when he rides behind someone, so that he does not fall. So its interpretation is: He will give you two shares that will protect you from the destruction of sins, just as the kifl protects the rider. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: (kiflayn) means "two times," in the language of Abyssinia. It is narrated from Ibn Zayd: (kiflayn) means the reward of this world and the Hereafter. It was also said: When the verse ﴿Those will be given their reward twice, because they were patient﴾ was revealed, the believers among the People of the Book boasted over the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, so this verse was revealed. Some scholars have used this verse to argue that a good deed earns only the reward of one like deed. They said: "Hasanah" (good deed) is a general term that applies to every kind of faith, and when the word hasanah is applied to one kind, the reward for it is only the equivalent of one. But if it applies to a good deed that comprises two kinds, the reward for it is double, based on this verse, for He said: (two portions of His mercy), and the kifl is a share, like an equivalent. So He granted the one who fears Allah and believes in His Messenger two portions: one portion for fear of Allah, and one portion for his faith in His Messenger. This shows that the good deed for which ten (rewards) are given is the one that gathers ten kinds of good deeds, and that is faith, which Allah, may He be exalted, has described as comprising ten kinds, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women﴾, the verse in its entirety. So these ten kinds are the ones whose rewards are their equivalents, and so each kind has one equivalent. This is a corrupt interpretation, because it departs from the general sense of the apparent meaning in His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like of it﴾ [[See vol. 14, p. 187]], in a way that the specification of the general does not permit, because whatever comprises ten good deeds is not repaid, for each good deed, except with its like. It is also invalid that the reward of a good deed is ten times its like, and the reports indicate this, and they have already been mentioned [[See vol. 7, p. 150 and vol. 13, p. 244]]. And if it were as was stated, there would be no difference between a good deed and an evil deed.

(And He will make for you a light) by which you walk, meaning clarification and guidance, according to Mujahid. Ibn Abbas said: it is the Qur'an. It was also said: it is light. (By which you walk) in the Hereafter, on the Sirat (bridge), and on the Day of Resurrection, to Paradise. It was also said: by which you walk among the people, calling them to Islam, so that you will be leaders in the religion of Islam, and your leadership, which you held, will not be removed from you. This is because they feared that their leadership would be lost if they believed in Muhammad, peace be upon him. What they would have lost was only the taking of a small bribe from the weak, by distorting the rulings of Allah, not genuine leadership in religion.

(And He will forgive you) your sins, (and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So that the People of the Book may know﴾. That is, so that he may know. (An la) is an additional, emphasizing particle, as said by al-Akhfash. Al-Farra' said: its meaning is "so that he may know," and (la) is an additional particle in every statement in which a negation occurs. Qatadah said: The People of the Book envied the Muslims, so this was revealed: (So that the People of the Book may know), that is, so that the People of the Book may know that they (do not have power over anything of Allah's bounty, and that bounty is in the hand of Allah). Mujahid said: The Jews said, "Soon a prophet will arise from among us who will cut off hands and feet." When he came from the Arabs, they disbelieved, so this was revealed: (So that), that is, so that the People of the Book may know (that they do not have power), meaning that they do have power, like His saying: ﴿that it does not return to them a word﴾ [[See vol. 11, p. 236]]. From al-Hasan: (Layla yaʿlama ahl al-kitab), and this was narrated from Ibn Mujahid. Qutrub narrated it with a kasra on the lam and sukun on the ya' [[Qutrub narrated it from al-Hasan as well, as in al-Samin and others, so al-Hasan has two readings: with fatha on the lam and with kasra on the lam, both with sukun on the ya']]. The fatha on the lam of the preposition is well known. The reason for the sukun on the ya' is that the hamza of (an) was dropped, so it became (lan), then the nun was assimilated into the lam, so it became (lilla). When the lams came together, the middle one was changed into a ya', as they say in (amma): ayma. **Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 57, verses 28–29:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who believe﴾, meaning: believe in Musa and Isa. (Fear Allah and believe in His Messenger), meaning Muhammad ﷺ. (He will give you a double portion of His mercy), meaning two shares of reward for your faith in Isa and Muhammad, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon them both. This is like His saying: ﴿Those will be given their reward twice, because they were patient﴾. The discussion of this has already been covered [[See vol. 13, p. 297]]. Al-kifl (the double portion) means share and portion. It was discussed in (al-Nisa') [[See vol. 4, p. 295]]. Originally it is a cloth that the rider wraps around himself so that he is not thrown off. This was said by Ibn Juraij. Al-Azhari said something similar, saying: its derivation is from the cloth that a camel rider wraps around its hump when he rides behind someone, so that he does not fall. So its interpretation is: He will give you two shares that will protect you from the destruction of sins, just as the kifl protects the rider. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: (kiflayn) means "two times," in the language of Abyssinia. It is narrated from Ibn Zayd: (kiflayn) means the reward of this world and the Hereafter. It was also said: When the verse ﴿Those will be given their reward twice, because they were patient﴾ was revealed, the believers among the People of the Book boasted over the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, so this verse was revealed. Some scholars have used this verse to argue that a good deed earns only the reward of one like deed. They said: "Hasanah" (good deed) is a general term that applies to every kind of faith, and when the word hasanah is applied to one kind, the reward for it is only the equivalent of one. But if it applies to a good deed that comprises two kinds, the reward for it is double, based on this verse, for He said: (two portions of His mercy), and the kifl is a share, like an equivalent. So He granted the one who fears Allah and believes in His Messenger two portions: one portion for fear of Allah, and one portion for his faith in His Messenger. This shows that the good deed for which ten (rewards) are given is the one that gathers ten kinds of good deeds, and that is faith, which Allah, may He be exalted, has described as comprising ten kinds, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women﴾, the verse in its entirety. So these ten kinds are the ones whose rewards are their equivalents, and so each kind has one equivalent. This is a corrupt interpretation, because it departs from the general sense of the apparent meaning in His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like of it﴾ [[See vol. 14, p. 187]], in a way that the specification of the general does not permit, because whatever comprises ten good deeds is not repaid, for each good deed, except with its like. It is also invalid that the reward of a good deed is ten times its like, and the reports indicate this, and they have already been mentioned [[See vol. 7, p. 150 and vol. 13, p. 244]]. And if it were as was stated, there would be no difference between a good deed and an evil deed.

(And He will make for you a light) by which you walk, meaning clarification and guidance, according to Mujahid. Ibn Abbas said: it is the Qur'an. It was also said: it is light. (By which you walk) in the Hereafter, on the Sirat (bridge), and on the Day of Resurrection, to Paradise. It was also said: by which you walk among the people, calling them to Islam, so that you will be leaders in the religion of Islam, and your leadership, which you held, will not be removed from you. This is because they feared that their leadership would be lost if they believed in Muhammad, peace be upon him. What they would have lost was only the taking of a small bribe from the weak, by distorting the rulings of Allah, not genuine leadership in religion.
